title: What If Night on the Moon Lasted Two Weeks? Your Base Would Freeze
subject: lunar surface

scenes.text: What if you built a Moon base? The Sun sets, and it doesn't rise for two weeks.
At the equator, the Moon's daytime surface can climb to about 120 degrees Celsius. That is hotter than boiling water.
With no air to hold heat, the ground drops fast once the Sun sets. Night falls below minus 130 Celsius.
Solar panels make nothing for roughly 14 Earth days, so a base needs stored heat, batteries, or nuclear power.
Near the poles, some craters never see sunlight at all. They can fall to about minus 250 Celsius, among the coldest places known in the solar system.
That is why ESA studies using lunar soil to store daytime heat for the night. The Moon gives you light and cold in equal measure.

description:
What if you built a base on the Moon and the Sun set for two weeks?
The surface swings from about 120 Celsius by day to below minus 130 at night, and some polar craters never see sunlight.
